nb(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C2).
mk(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !nb(Y, X).
ya(min(Y)) :- mk(Y, X).
yb(max(Y)) :- mk(Y, X).
xa(min(X)) :- mk(Y, X).
xb(max(X)) :- mk(Y, X).
inside(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), ya(A), yb(B), xa(P), xb(Q), Y > A, Y < B, X > P, X < Q.

inner(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), ya(A), yb(B), xa(P), xb(Q), Y > A, Y < B, X > P, X < Q.

reading: Each 1 cup (rectangle outline with a gap in its top edge) holds one coloured cell; its interior, the gap and the row just above the cup are filled with that colour.

new_rows.name: cupreg
new_rows.datalog:
one(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 1.
cup(O) :- obj(O, Y, X), one(Y, X).
by0(O, min(Y)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
by1(O, max(Y)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
bx0(O, min(X)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
bx1(O, max(X)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
cupreg(Y, X) :- by0(O, A), by1(O, B), bx0(O, P), bx1(O, Q), A1 = A - 1, px(Y, X, C), Y >= A1, Y <= B, X >= P, X <= Q, !one(Y, X).

why: for each cup, every non-1 cell in its box extended one row up takes the colour of the seed cell inside it

reading: A dashed 1 figure (rectangle plus possibly an inner line) is completed: every gap on a row or column that is one of the figure's lines, inside the figure's bounding box, is filled with 2.

new_rows.name: gaps
new_rows.datalog:
ya(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
yb(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
xa(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
xb(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rc(Y, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
cc(X, count(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
lrow(Y) :- rc(Y, N), N >= 4.
lcol(X) :- cc(X, N), N >= 4.
gaps(Y, X) :- lrow(Y), px(Y, X, C), C = 0, xa(P), xb(Q), X >= P, X <= Q.
gaps(Y, X) :- lcol(X), px(Y, X, C), C = 0, ya(A), yb(B), Y >= A, Y <= B.

why: rows/columns holding at least 4 one-cells are the figure's lines; all their background cells within the figure's box become 2, nothing else changes
